items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Billy May had me featured behind Nat Cole; I was playing like an obbligato on the tuba to the bridge of 'Once In A While.'

ctx.x: You mentioned that Wellman Braud was playing bass when you first saw him.

Yeah, I'm thinking it must have been at the Savoy Ballroom, or some ballroom in Harlem or in New York. Because there used to be a lot of dances. That's the first place I saw Noble Sissle's band; I think it was the Rockland Palace. Well, it could have been the Rockland Palace that I first saw Duke. And that's where I first saw Nat Cole's brother, even though I didn't know Nat at the time. Eddie

items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Nat used to pick me up sometimes... This was before Nat became... Well, he had his trio, but he wasn't, you know, the millionaire Nat King Cole. He was just ordinary Nat King Cole, the piano player, at that point.

ctx.x: Was there a regular broadcast from that Billy Berg's?

We used to broadcast every night. But these jam sessions naturally weren't broadcasted. And that's where Norman Granz first came in the picture. I think Norman was still going to school. He used to come in his tennis shoes. And I think this gave Norman the idea for the Jazz concerts. Because we used to do...Sunday afternoons we used to... There was a place on Normandie and Jefferson, Normandie Hall, and we used to do sessions there. I remember one day... Nat used to pick me up sometimes. He had an, I'd say, old…
What year would that have been?
